newsitem.title: UK: Wall St lifts Euroshares to closing highs.
newsitem.headline: Wall St lifts Euroshares to closing highs.

text.p: Europe's key bourses surged to new closing highs on Friday when Wall Street rose strongly again after two days of 80-point gains.
"We've seen a great performance today, which should restore confidence to a worried market," one trader in London said.
London, Europe's biggest bourse, rose 47.4 points, or 1.21 percent, to close at a record 4,275.8 points, up 57 points since the start of the week.
When London closed, Wall Street was up 33 points after digesting stronger than expected fourth quarter U.S. gross domestic product data showing annualised growth of 4.7 percent.
U.S. traders concentrated on other inflation measures in the GDP report which suggested the rate of price rises remained generally in check, a factor which pushed U.S. bonds higher.

London traders said the fate of the market next week depended on monetary meetings in both Britain and the United States. An interest rate hike on either side of the Atlantic could bring the FTSE tumbling back down to earth, they said.
"It could still be a white-knuckle ride next week," the London trader said.
The spectre of a sharp sell-off sparked by a U.S. rate rise will keep markets nervous ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee rate policy meeting on February 4 and 5, dealers said.
February 4 is the third anniversary of an unexpected U.S interest rate hike which sent world stock markets reeling. Some analysts believe history could repeat itself.

Robert Buckland, UK equity strategist at HSBC James Capel, said the market was divided over whether U.S. rates would rise. "It's a fateful anniversary," he said. "On balance we're not expecting a rate rise but its definitely quite a close call."
Nerves will be further frayed by Britain's monthly monetary meeting on Wednesday, which could result in a rate rise.
Higher interest rates would sorely test the world's share markets, many of which are at or near record levels, by making returns on alternative investments and cash more attractive.
In Paris, the CAC 40 index was up 13.50, or 0.54 percent, at 2,516.56, a new record. It rose 3.5 percent during the week.
Alcatel Alsthom ended up 4.78 percent at 548 francs, having forecast a spectacular rebound to a profit of 2.5 billion francs for 1996 from a loss of 25.6 billion in 1995.

In Frankfurt, the DAX index closed up 17.83 points, or 0.59 percent, at 3,035.15, also a new record. The DAX IBIS ended up 19.12 points at 3,037.70, having set an intraday high in pre-bourse screen trade of 3,050.88 points.
SAP rose nearly 11 percent after the blue-chip software group shocked the market by beating its own results forecasts for 1996. Porsche also rose 10.5 percent, after announcing strong profits.

The dollar steadied in late Europe after a volatile session as the market absorbed the U.S. economic data. By 1700 gmt, it was worth 1.6360 marks and 121.10 yen, a touch down from Thursday's late European levels.
"It's the same old story -- strong growth, but subdued inflation," said John Calverley, chief economist and strategist at American Express Bank in London.
While strong, the figures would not change the U.S. interest rate outlook, analysts said.

"The dollar is just sort of consolidating," said Peter von Maydell, senior currency economist at UBS. "Today's data is just an excuse to maintain that," he said, adding that many dealers had taken profits and closed their books for the month.

The pound was also vulnerable after heavy selling against the dollar and yen spilled over into mark trade. There were signs that British interest rates may not rise as soon as expected, traders said. In late trade, the pound was at $1.5995 and 2.6185 marks. Gold remained weak in the afternoon, closing at $344.60, its lowest for 3-1/4 years. It has plunged from about $370 at the start of the year, haaving been shunned by investors who prefer to pour money into the booming the U.S. stock market.
CURRENCIES AT 1700 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6360 marks and 121.10 yen, compared with late Thursday's European levels of 1.6382 marks and 121.61 yen.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING PRICES
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading shares was up 47.4 points at 4,275.8.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 13.50 points at 2,516.56. FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 17.83 points at 3,035.15.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $344.60, down sharply from Thursday's close in Europe of $347.35.
